Brand exploration · round 2

Seven new directions

Unlike round 1, these do not start from the palace illustration. Each one has its own symbol, colours and fonts, to show how differently Mithai Palace could look. Each is shown on its light and dark colours, at icon size, and with its colours and fonts listed. You can also mix ideas: for example the jalebi M with the maroon and gold you already use.

Direction A

Kaju katli diamond

The symbol is a kaju katli: a maroon diamond covered in crinkled silver leaf (varq), with an M in the middle. It feels premium and modern, and silver replaces gold, which sets you apart from the many maroon-and-gold sweet shops. Best for: gift boxes (silver foil on maroon card looks very expensive), social media and signage.

Type: Cinzel + Cormorant Garamond
Light
Dark
Icon · 64 / 32 / 16 px
Direction B

Jalebi M

An M drawn as one piped jalebi line, with a curl at each end and a glossy syrup highlight. It is warm, handmade and friendly, and shows that sweets are made here. Best for: a shop that wants to feel welcoming rather than formal; it is also very memorable on Instagram and delivery apps.

Type: Yeseva One + Inter
Light
Dark
Icon · 64 / 32 / 16 px
Direction C

Crown of ladoos

"Palace" becomes royalty: a gold crown with a boondi ladoo on each point and the four-petal flower from your current logo. It keeps the regal feel with a much simpler symbol. Shown in royal plum and gold for contrast, but it would also work in your maroon. Best for: festive and wedding orders.

Type: Cinzel
Light
Dark
Icon · 64 / 32 / 16 px
Direction D

Jharokha window

A Rajasthani palace window with a gold lattice screen (jaali) and a canopy on top: a quieter kind of "palace". The peacock teal is unusual for a sweet shop, which makes it stand out on a busy street and complements the colours of the mithai. Best for: a calm, upmarket café-sweet-shop look.

Type: Marcellus + Cormorant Garamond
Light
Dark
Icon · 64 / 32 / 16 px
Direction E

Vintage halwai signboard

Bold, colourful Bombay-style shop signage: rani pink, marigold and bottle green, with the name in Hindi above the English. Nostalgic and fun, and the kind of sign people photograph. Best for: the shopfront, a street-food or chaat counter, and bold social media posts. The icon is the Hindi letter म.

Type: Rozha One (Latin + Devanagari) + Inter
Light
Dark
Icon · 64 / 32 / 16 px
Direction F

Modern boutique

A modern patisserie look: the name in lowercase, a soft pink ladoo with pistachio slivers as the symbol, and pink, pistachio and cocoa colours. It looks like a modern dessert shop and appeals to younger and non-Indian customers. Best for: making mithai feel like a fashionable gift, much like macarons. The biggest change from your current look.

Type: Fraunces + Inter
Light
Dark
Icon · 64 / 32 / 16 px
Direction G

Hindi-first with toran

मिठाई is the main text, with a marigold garland (toran) above like a shop decorated for Diwali, and "PALACE" underneath in English. It is proudly Indian and works for both Hindi and English readers. Best for: an authentic, community-favourite feel. Confirm the Hindi spelling and lettering with the owner.

Type: Rozha One + Cinzel + Inter
